::: {.digest-item}
**[Genie: Generative Interactive Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15391)**

<span class="digest-source">arXiv · DeepMind</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> A foundation model that turns a single image into an interactive, steerable world — it generates plausible next frames in response to actions, rather than just predicting forward. It is the first general-purpose "world model" that can be *played*, and the template for how DeepMind frames world modeling as a pretraining objective.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> The canonical recent reference for world models. A useful contrast to how "world models" are framed in telecom/6G literature — the word means very different things in the two fields.

<span class="digest-tags">#world-models · #deepmind</span>
:::

::: {.digest-item}
**[World Labs](https://worldlabs.ai/)**

<span class="digest-source">World Labs</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> Fei-Fei Li's "spatial intelligence" lab — building generative models that produce rich, interactive 3D worlds instead of flat images or text. The bet is that understanding space (geometry, physics, persistence) is the next frontier after language.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> A signal of where world models are heading commercially — beyond text into spatial and physical simulation.

<span class="digest-tags">#world-models · #spatial-intelligence</span>
:::

::: {.digest-item}
**[Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models Into Concepts](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2023/monosemantic-features/index.html)**

<span class="digest-source">Anthropic</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> Uses sparse autoencoders to decompose LLM activations into thousands of interpretable, mostly single-concept features. This is the paper that kicked off the modern interpretability wave — and the methodological template (SAE + feature analysis) that most follow-up work builds on.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> Foundational for mechanistic interpretability. The feature-decomposition lens maps well onto asking "what is the network actually doing" in slice management.

<span class="digest-tags">#interpretability · #llm</span>
:::

::: {.digest-item}
**[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)**

<span class="digest-source">GitHub</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> A minimal C/C++ runtime for LLM inference on CPUs and consumer hardware — the engine behind most local inference stacks. Its GGML quantization formats are what make 7B+ models runnable on a laptop or an edge box, with no GPU required.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> The practical foundation for local/edge inference experiments. Skim the README and quantization docs to ground edge-inference thinking.

<span class="digest-tags">#edge-inference · #local-llm</span>
:::
